text:
Partly. Satellite evidence shows tree-cover loss of about 0.6 ha (3.4% of the 17.6 ha property) in 2022, and it is corroborated. The Hansen/UMD data detected it, a later year (up to 2025) was observed, and the JRC 2020 map agrees the area was forest. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 0.5 ha of the lost area as native forest, 0.1 ha as outside mapped forest, and none as planted forest. A further 0.2 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

However, the evidence does not establish that deforestation or land-use change occurred. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvest, fire or storm. It also does not show the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance finding (e.g., EUDR status).

So: native-forest tree-cover loss in 2022 is supported, but "deforestation" is not confirmed.
